'''Brigitte Vallée''' (née Salesse) (born 6 June 1950, in Courbevoie, Hauts-de-Seine, France) is a French [[mathematician]] and [[computer scientist]]. She entered the [[École Normale Supérieure]] de Jeunes Filles in 1970, and received her PhD in 1986 at the University of Caen (Lattice reduction algorithms in small dimensions).<ref name=":0">{{Citation|title=Décret du 12 juillet 2013 portant promotion et nomination|url=https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/affichTexte.do?cidTexte=JORFTEXT000027697953&dateTexte=&categorieLien=id|access-date=2020-05-31}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=BnF.fr - Vallée|url=https://catalogue.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/cb122955843|last=|first=|date=|website=BnF|language=fr|access-date=2020-05-31}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web|title=Brigitte Vallée - The Mathematics Genealogy Project|url=https://genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=141579|website=genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu|access-date=2020-05-31}}</ref> Her doctoral advisor was [[Jacques Stern (cryptographer)|Jacques Stern]].<ref name=":2" />

Vallée has been Director of Research at the French [[CNRS]] at [[Université de Caen]],<ref>{{Cite web|title=Annuaire|url=http://www.unicaen.fr/ufr/sciences/visualise.php?id=306|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070929153604/http://www.unicaen.fr/ufr/sciences/visualise.php?id=306|url-status=dead|archive-date=2007-09-29|date=2007-09-29|access-date=2020-05-31}}</ref> since 2001 and specialized in computational [[number theory]] and [[analysis of algorithms]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=EXCLUSIF. Le nouveau Conseil national du numérique dévoilé|url=https://o.nouvelobs.com/high-tech/20130117.OBS5805/exclusif-le-nouveau-conseil-national-du-numerique-devoile.html|website=O|date=19 January 2013 |language=fr|access-date=2020-05-31}}</ref> Amongst the algorithms she studied are the celebrated [[Lenstra–Lenstra–Lovász lattice basis reduction algorithm|LLL]] algorithm used for basis reductions in [[Lattice (group)|Euclidean lattice]] and the different [[Euclidean algorithm]]s to determine [[Greatest common divisor|GCD]]. The main tool used to achieve her results is the so-called ''dynamical analysis''. Loosely speaking, it is a mix between analysis of algorithms and dynamical systems. Brigitte Vallée greatly contributed to the development of this method.

In the early 90s, Brigitte Vallée's work on small modular squares allowed her to hold the fastest [[factorisation]] algorithm with a proved probabilistic complexity bound. Nowadays, other factorisation algorithms are faster.

She was appointed a knight of the [[Legion of Honour|Legion of Honor]] by the Ministry of Higher Education and Research on 12 July 2013.<ref name=":0" />

==Selected publications==
According to [[Zentralblatt MATH|zbMath]], Vallée has authored 88 publications since 1986, including 3 books.<ref>{{Cite web|title=zbMATH - the first resource for mathematics|url=https://zbmath.org/authors/?q=ai:vallee.brigitte|website=zbmath.org|access-date=2020-05-31}}</ref>
* Brigitte Vallée, ''Generation of Elements with Small Modular Squares and Provably Fast Integer Factoring Algorithms'', Mathematics of Computation, Vol. 56, No. 194 (Apr., 1991), pp.&nbsp;823–849.
*Brigitte Vallée, ''Algorithmique en géométrie des nombres. Applications à la cryptographie et à la factorisation des entiers'' (''A geometric approach to the reduction of small-scale networks)'', 1986 [University thesis]<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" />
